> Currently, there is no way to tie this kind of disclaimer to a specific instance.

The code for this already exists in VRChat... for worlds. It was used for Furality Somna. It currently requires VRChat Team to set a world tag for each world: `admin_url_consent_furality_somna`

See also tupper's response there: https://ask.vrchat.com/t/developer-update-december-18-2025/47354/58

> If [the present authority] can’t [ensure that everyone that joins consents] in a Group Plus? Then don’t run a Group Plus. They should run a Group-only (AV, of course) instance and put the consent statement/inform into the rules where people see it. Alternately, they could use a custom world that has a disclaimer on join, that requires a button press to pass.

Several public VRChat rave groups (which shall be unnamed for now, if you know then you know) I've witnessed have already operated successfully as group-only/group+ (in Age Gated instances) for a long time by including a disclaimer or a set of expectations for an event on join with a button press in a custom world (after the world has been loaded). A custom world that does this doesn't entirely eliminate the issue of lingering users at the spawn point or the few users ignoring the disclaimer at spawn (anecdotally ~10% of attendees at a rave venue from my experience, twice a month), but it's better than nothing.

At worst, such disclaimers on world load may turn into user fatiguing "consent prompts weaponized" (or the so-called "cookie fatigue" phenomenon, where users become desensitized or exhausted by repeated consent requests as seen on a majority of big websites today), if those consent/disclaimer/rules prompts are tied to an instance instead of a group's rules that you need to accept once when you join the group.

@{68098a4626271974ef4d2775|full_name} All the current solutions work if implemented, but only so far and not in a way that's tied to a system, as far as I understand. 

Which is to say, if one of these VRC rave groups, for example, makes a custom world for their events that includes such a disclaimer at spawn, that may work for them, in that world. It depends on whether that's accepted as consent and taken into account in the event of a report on the conduct at that event.

However, that depends on the group creating their own world, and/or having a dedicated world for events that would require that sort of disclaimer.

Tying that message to the instance, rather than the world or the group or the event description, eliminates all or most of the potential situations in which someone could end up in an instance while saying they did not see or agree to the content or conduct within.

In terms of the importance of gathering consent from people who join the instance, we need a clear way we can do that before someone actually joins the instance, and also preferably one that can be logged for purposes of adjudicating reports.

details:
The December 18th Developer Update included some clarifying language regarding private instances and the consent of those in those instances WRT whatever activities are taking place there. They included an example of group rules written to gather the consent of those joining the group.

Currently, there is no way to tie this kind of disclaimer to a specific instance. It can be tied to a group or an event, but not an instance. My request is for group instance creators to be able to enable and set a dialog box on instance creation that can contain things like event rules, avatar restrictions, or a description of the event's content, that users would have to agree to before joining the world.

This would make it easier for users to understand what kind of event they're getting into, and would make it easier for groups and event organizers to make sure everyone in the instance is comfortable with what's going on.
title: Add the option to set a disclaimer/rules/description dialog to group instances.
